title: Extending SLMJury
blurb: Add a judge, a student, a dataset or a persona.

blocks.html: New judges, students, datasets and personas plug into the same pipeline, so every runner and analysis picks them up by key.

items: Add an entry under judge_models (small) or large_judge_models (large) in slmjury/configs/models.yaml. The key is the name you pass on the command line.
Set model to the Hugging Face repository, and tensor_parallel_size to the number of GPUs it needs. The other fields are described on Models and models.yaml.
If the model thinks before answering, set enable_thinking: true. If it cannot stop thinking, also set always_thinks: true, and the runners skip the 10-token budget for it.

blocks.code:
python scripts/run_judge.py --judge my-judge-7b --max-tokens 10 8192
python scripts/run_evaluation.py --judge my-judge-7b --summary
python scripts/run_scoring_judge.py --judge my-judge-7b --datasets summeval

blocks.html: scripts/run_judge.py looks a key up in judge_models first and then in large_judge_models, so a large judge needs nothing else. Write its outputs next to the other large judges with --output-dir results/large_judges.
Add an entry under student_models with the same fields, then run python scripts/run_student.py --student <key>. Judges grade any student whose solutions are in results/core/student_solutions/<key>/.

items: Write a loader in slmjury/data/<name>.py that returns a list of dicts with problem_id, question, ground_truth_reasoning and ground_truth_answer. The existing loaders download from Hugging Face once and cache the JSON under data/.
Register it in DATASET_LOADERS in slmjury/data/__init__.py, so load_dataset("<name>") finds it.

Map its name to an answer type in get_dataset_type() in slmjury/parsers/answer.py: numeric, latex or multiple_choice. The type picks the student prompt, the answer extraction and the comparison with the reference.
Run a student and a judge on it with --datasets <name>.

blocks.html: Personas are system prompts. Add one to the PERSONAS dictionary in slmjury/strategies/persona.py, and scripts/run_persona.py runs it with the others, or alone with --personas <Name>. The current six are on the Prompts page.

JudgeModel.evaluate_batch() takes prompt_template, a string with the fields {question}, {ground_truth} and {student_answer}. The prompt-sensitivity experiment keeps its rewordings in slmjury/configs/prompt_variants.yaml, and experiments/prompt_sensitivity/run_prompt_variants.py --variant <name> runs one of them.
